notes.title: Patch 3 - Quality of Life
notes.content:
This update addresses a few of the long term issues that were pointed out by player's who've finished the game.

[b]- Stamina Cost per tick while Sprinting was changed from 6 -> 3
- Sprinting is now slightly faster overall.[/b]

~ A common point of feedback was the stamina system seeming a bit unnecessary when traversing the open-world. Rather than remove it, stamina recovery and cost has been tweaked so that as long as you've collected a few batteries you shouldn't have to stop and recover nearly as much.

- Several softlocks fixed
- Various unintended puzzle skips fixed
- Popup text moves faster to make it less tedious if you decide not to skip it
- Various geometry tweaks in the world
- Some changes to text in UI and menus for readability

notes.title: Patch 1 - March 17th
notes.content:
Hello players! I want to thank everyone for their support during this launch window. 

This is the first of a series of patches intended to improve the experience for users on Steam and bring the game more in line with this platform rather than the platform it originally launched on. 

- Improvements to the way mouse and joystick is handled so that people playing purely with controller should have a better experience
- Several softlocks addressed
- Scrapyard boss has had AI improved to match other enemies in the game
- Culling / Draw distance increased in every environment (A slider to be added at a later date)
- Objects like the red-doors have had their culling settings changed so that they don't flicker
- F12 (Steam screenshot button) no longer hides the HUD, it's been remapped to F10
- Other small visual updates

There is more to come, I've been listening to feedback about things like stamina and visual animation blending and am working out solutions to address them without making the game unstable. I am a solo developer and so I tend to be fairly cautious with major fixes as stability is a big focus for this game.

notes.title: End's Reach - Launching March 7th, 2025 - Windows, Linux and Mac OS
notes.content:
Hello everyone, 

First off, I am excited to say that End's Reach will release onto Windows, Linux, and Mac on March 7th.

[h2]What is "End's Reach"? [/h2]
End's Reach is an action-adventure game inspired by the late 90s and early 2000s era. The games I looked to for guidance were Metroid Prime and The Legend of Zelda - but the game ended up falling somewhere in between into unique territory. While it may not be the most 'PC focused' genre, I feel it's right at home on a Steamdeck and I hope the Steam community grows to love it the way that the Atari VCS community do. 

Since I was a young boy in the 90's I have always dreamed of building an open-world and populating it with enemies, puzzles, and dungeons. After slogging through the mobile-game and app industry for several years I took the plunge of making my first full commercial game, and here it is.

[h2]Not an Early-Access[/h2]
I do not believe in taking money for something that isn't ready to be sold. This is not an Early-Access period, the game has been in development since 2019 and released onto it's original platform in 2023. You're playing a tested version of the game that hundreds of players have already beaten. [b]Your money does not go to a publisher or a corporation,[/b] it goes directly to the developer to support future games. The Atari VCS received 3 major updates over the last year, and the Steam version is the most definitive release of End's Reach to date. 

I hope everyone has a good time with the game, it will be on a 10% discount for it's launch week. 

Thanks for your support and thank you for playing.
